copy.blurb:
Brazil face Haiti on Saturday, overnight UTC kickoff, in FIFA World Cup 2026. This is one of the matches where the model's number disagrees with the closing line on Polymarket — a narrow gap on the the draw side, +4.1pp.

On Elo, Brazil comes in 520 points ahead — Brazil at 1970, Haiti at 1450. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Brazil to win at 86%, the draw at 10%, and Haiti to win at 4%. The draw side reads 10% on this distribution — the model's central case for the draw.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Brazil to win at 92%, the draw at 6%, and Haiti to win at 3%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the the draw side — 6% on the market, 10% on the engine, a +4.1pp gap.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On the draw the lower bound is 10%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +4.1pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding the draw priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 28 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read. Per The Guardian (football): "He will be an important player in this World Cup." France 24 (sport, EN) carried the same line: "Brazil superstar Neymar was handed a dramatic recall to the country's World Cup squad on Monday, returning to the national team after a…"
drivers: Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the the draw side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives the draw a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.

copy.summary: The model and the market disagree on whether a stalemate is in play here. Our prior puts the draw at 10%; Polymarket prices it at 6%. The +4.1pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Brazil v Haiti · the model leans the draw
